docs.title: Technical Stack Overview
docs.text: Layer Technology Frontend React 19 + Vite 8 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 Backend Express 5 + TypeScript + Zod validation Database PostgreSQL hosted on Neon, accessed via Prisma ORM 7 Auth JWT + email verification + optional TOTP 2FA with recovery codes (otplib + qrcode) + rate limiting Email Resend (preferred) / Gmail SMTP via nodemailer (fallback) Notifications Web push (web-push) with a service worker Shared @logbook/shared — TypeScript interfaces and Zod schemas consumed by both frontend and backend Testing Vitest + Supertest (backend), Vitest + Testing Library (frontend) — see Testing Linting oxlint (frontend) / TypeScript type checker (backend) Workspace Monorepo using npm workspaces

docs.title: Sprint 1 Summary
docs.text:
Sprint 1 delivers the core logbook functionality with authentication and user management:

  • Authentication — Registration, login, JWT tokens, email verification, password reset, and account deletion.
  • Two-Factor Authentication — TOTP-based 2FA with QR code setup, enable/disable flow in Settings.
  • Project Management — Create, edit, archive/unarchive projects with unique name enforcement per user.
  • Entry Schema Definition — Define custom entry fields (TEXT, NUMBER, DATE, BOOLEAN) per project.
  • Entry CRUD — Create, update, delete logbook entries with typed field values, due dates, and backdated entry dates.
  • Time Tracking — Record duration per entry, view per-project time summaries (total hours, entry count, last entry).
  • Project Detail View — Entry format section (required/optional indicators), grouped entries by date, clean modal form for entry creation.
  • Entry Browser — Vertical timeline layout with date grouping, search, project filter, entry type filter (All/This Week/Overdue), and newest/oldest sort toggle.
  • Overdue Entries — Entries past due_date flagged with red border, warning badge, and dedicated Overdue filter tab.
  • Profile Page — Avatar upload, bio/slogan, degree, year, and student number with edit mode.
  • Settings — Account management, 2FA setup, dark/light theme, notification preferences, logbook preferences, and data export/import (JSON/CSV).
  • Auth UI — Full-screen animated canvas background with floating particles, light streaks, and logbook icons. Frosted-glass form cards.
  • API Testing — 27 Vitest integration tests covering all endpoints against the live database.
  • Responsive Design — Tailwind CSS v4 design system with dark mode, collapsible sidebar, and mobile-friendly layout.

docs.title: Sprint 2 Summary
docs.text:
Sprint 2 builds on the Sprint 1 foundation (authentication, project management, entry CRUD, dashboard, and settings) with richer entry formatting, deeper analytics, offline support, and cross-feature integration.

  • Rich Field Types — Support for tags, checklists, links, and references as entry field types, extending the original TEXT/NUMBER/DATE/BOOLEAN set.
  • Entry Format Editing — Add, remove, and rename fields on an existing project's entry format after creation.
  • Entry Format Versioning — Preserve previous versions of an entry format so historical entries remain valid and readable after schema changes.
  • Computed Fields — Define fields whose values are calculated automatically from other fields in the same entry.
  • Custom Field Analytics — Totals, grouping, comparisons, and plotting/visualization of data captured in custom fields.
  • Alternative Views — Calendar view and board (kanban-style) view for browsing entries beyond the existing timeline layout.
  • Unfinished Work & Due Date Tracking — Dedicated tracking for outstanding/unfinished entries and their due dates, building on Sprint 1's overdue flagging.
  • Offline Entry Capture — Create and save entries locally without a connection, with sync to the server once back online.
  • Data Export & Import (Extended) — Expanded export/import functionality for logbook data, building on Sprint 1's JSON/CSV support.
  • Cross-Feature Integration & Testing — Integration of all Sprint 2 features into a cohesive whole, end-to-end testing across features, resolution of cross-feature bugs, and regression testing against Sprint 1 functionality.

docs.title: Sprint 2 Ownership
docs.text: Area Owner User Stories Entry Formats & Fields Person 1 US07 – Rich Field Types, US08 – Modify Entry Format, US09 – Preserve Format Versions, US10 – Computed Fields Statistics & Views Person 2 US11 – Analyse Custom Fields, US12 – Alternative Views, US13 – Track Unfinished Work & Due Dates Offline & Data Person 3 US14 – Capture Entries Offline, US15 – Export & Import Logbook Data Integration & Testing Person 4 Integration of all features, cross-feature testing, bug fixing, regression testing against Sprint 1, floating support to whichever area needs it

docs.title: Sprint 3 Summary
docs.text:
Sprint 3 delivers the Advanced logbook: computing over data whose shape only its owner knows, a record that is hard to lose, a logbook that does some of the writing itself, and staying quick as the record grows. Stories are numbered as on the Sprint 3 board.

  • Custom Expressions & Saved Statistics (US22, US23) — Write an expression such as SUM({Hours}) / COUNT() over your own entries and save it beside the built-in statistics.
  • Entry Automation Rules (US24) — Rules that add or remove tags or set the status when an entry is created or saved.
  • Custom Dashboard (US25, US26) — Choose and arrange statistics and information panels, including saved statistics; the layout is stored on the server, so it is the same on every device.
  • Recurring Entries (US27) — Entries that repeat daily, weekly or monthly.
  • Automatic Reminders (US28) — Reminders for upcoming and overdue due dates, stalled entries and daily logging, delivered as push notifications even with the logbook closed.
  • Entry Version History (US29–US31) — Every change is kept; view an entry as it was on any date, and restore an earlier version.
  • Archiving & Performance (US32, US33) — Archive old entries out of the way; database indexes, a paginated Entries page and one request for open work.
  • Advanced Search (US35–US37) — Searching inside custom fields, combining filters and ranking results; still in the Sprint 3 backlog.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
This page documents every endpoint exposed by the Digital Logbook backend API. All endpoints are prefixed with /api and return JSON responses.

Base URL (production): https://digital-logbook-backend-latest.onrender.com/api — a prefix, not an endpoint: request a path under it, such as /api/health.

Authentication: Most endpoints require a JWT in the Authorization: Bearer <token> header. Obtain one via the POST /api/auth/login endpoint.

docs.title: GET /api/health
docs.text:
Returns service health status. No authentication required.

Response 200: 

{ "status": "ok" }

docs.title: GET /api/db-check
docs.text:
Verifies database connectivity. No authentication required.

Response 200: 

{ "status": "ok", "message": "Successfully connected to Neon PostgreSQL via Prisma", "time": "2026-09-28T14:00:00.000Z" }

docs.title: POST /api/auth/register
docs.text:
Create a new user account.

Field Type Required Notes fullName string Yes email string Yes Must be a valid email; unique password string Yes Min 8 chars, at least one uppercase letter and one digit

Response 201: 

{ "message": "User registered successfully. Email auto-verified (dev mode).", "user": { "id": "...", "fullName": "...", "email": "..." } }
Errors: 409 (duplicate email), 400 (validation failure)

docs.title: POST /api/auth/verify-email
docs.text:
Verify a user's email address with the token sent during registration.

Field Type Required token string Yes

Response 200: { "message": "Email verified successfully." } Errors: 400 (invalid or expired token)

docs.title: POST /api/auth/login
docs.text:
Authenticate and receive a JWT. If 2FA is enabled, returns a flag instead of a token.

Field Type Required email string Yes password string Yes

Response 200 (no 2FA): 

{ "message": "Login successful", "token": "eyJ...", "user": { "id": "...", "fullName": "...", "email": "..." }, "scheduledDeletionAt": null }
scheduledDeletionAt is an ISO date when the account is inside its 30-day deletion grace period (see DELETE /api/auth/account), otherwise null. Logging in during the grace period does not cancel the deletion. Once the date has passed, the account is erased at the next login attempt, which then fails with 401 like an unknown email.

Response 200 (2FA enabled): 

{ "requiresTwoFactor": true, "email": "...", "twoFactorToken": "eyJ..." }
No session token is issued yet. twoFactorToken proves the password step succeeded; it is valid for five minutes and only for POST /api/auth/login/2fa.

Errors: 401 (wrong password or unknown email — identical message), 403 (unverified account), 429 (too many attempts)

docs.title: POST /api/auth/login/2fa
docs.text:
Complete sign-in after POST /api/auth/login returned requiresTwoFactor. The account is identified by twoFactorToken, not by an email address, so a code alone cannot sign anyone in.

Field Type Required twoFactorToken string Yes — from the login response code string Yes — a 6-digit TOTP code, or a recovery code (XXXXX-XXXXX)

Response 200: 

{ "message": "Login successful", "token": "eyJ...", "user": { "id": "...", "fullName": "...", "email": "..." }, "scheduledDeletionAt": null, "usedRecoveryCode": false, "recoveryCodesRemaining": 10 }
A recovery code works once. When one is used, usedRecoveryCode is true so the client can tell the user how many remain.

Errors: 400 (malformed request), 401 (invalid code, or the twoFactorToken has expired — sign in again), 429 (too many attempts)

docs.title: POST /api/auth/forgot-password
docs.text:
Request a password-reset email. Returns the same message regardless of whether the email exists (prevents account enumeration).

Field Type Required email string Yes

Response 200: 

{ "message": "If account exists, a reset link has been sent." }

docs.title: POST /api/auth/reset-password
docs.text:
Reset the password using a single-use token from the reset email.

Field Type Required token string Yes newPassword string Yes — same rules as registration

Response 200: { "message": "Password reset successfully." } Errors: 400 (invalid or expired token)

docs.title: DELETE /api/auth/account 🔒
docs.text:
Schedule the authenticated user's account for deletion. Nothing is removed straight away: the account enters a 30-day grace period, ending at midnight 30 days from the request, and a confirmation email is sent. The user can still log in during that time and can cancel with POST /api/auth/account/cancel-deletion. Once the period has ended, the account and all its data (projects, entries, values, tokens) are permanently deleted by the purge job, which runs when the server starts and then hourly, or at the next login attempt if that comes first.

Calling this again while a deletion is already scheduled keeps the original date and does not send another email.

Field Type Required confirmPassword string Yes

Response 200: 

{ "message": "Your account will be permanently deleted on Sat Oct 24 2026.", "scheduledDeletionAt": "2026-10-24T00:00:00.000Z" }
Errors: 400 (missing confirmPassword), 401 (wrong password), 404 (user not found)

docs.title: POST /api/auth/account/cancel-deletion 🔒
docs.text:
Cancel a scheduled account deletion during the grace period. No request body.

Response 200: { "message": "Account deletion cancelled." } Errors: 400 (no deletion is scheduled), 404 (user not found)

docs.title: POST /api/auth/2fa/setup 🔒
docs.text:
Begin 2FA setup — returns a TOTP secret and QR code data URL. The secret is stored encrypted, and 2FA is not switched on until verify-setup succeeds.

Response 200: 

{ "secret": "JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP", "qrCodeUrl": "data:image/png;base64,..." }
Errors: 400 (2FA already enabled), 404 (user not found), 503 (the server has no TWO_FACTOR_ENCRYPTION_KEY)

docs.title: POST /api/auth/2fa/verify-setup 🔒
docs.text:
Verify the TOTP code from the authenticator app to complete 2FA setup.

Field Type Required token string Yes — 6-digit TOTP code

Response 200: 

{ "message": "Two-factor authentication enabled successfully", "recoveryCodes": ["ABCDE-12345", "..."] }
The recovery codes are stored only as digests, so this response is the only time they can be read. The client must show them to the user now.

Errors: 400 (incorrect code, no setup in progress, or 2FA already enabled)

docs.title: POST /api/auth/2fa/disable 🔒
docs.text:
Disable 2FA. Requires password re-authentication. The secret and all recovery codes are removed.

Field Type Required password string Yes

Response 200: { "message": "Two-factor authentication disabled" } Errors: 400 (2FA not enabled), 401 (wrong password), 404 (user not found)

docs.title: POST /api/auth/2fa/recovery-codes 🔒
docs.text:
Replace the recovery codes with a new set. Every previous code stops working. Requires the password, so a borrowed session cannot mint itself a way back in.

Field Type Required password string Yes

Response 200: 

{ "message": "New recovery codes generated. Your previous codes no longer work.", "recoveryCodes": ["ABCDE-12345", "..."] }
Errors: 400 (2FA not enabled), 401 (wrong password), 404 (user not found)

docs.title: GET /api/auth/2fa/status 🔒
docs.text:
Check whether 2FA is enabled for the authenticated user, and how many recovery codes are left.

Response 200: 

{ "isTwoFactorEnabled": true, "recoveryCodesRemaining": 8, "recoveryCodeCount": 10 }

docs.title: POST /api/projects
docs.text:
Create a new project.

Field Type Required Notes name string Yes Unique per user description string No

Response 201: 

{ "id": "...", "name": "...", "description": "...", "status": "ACTIVE" }
Errors: 409 (duplicate name), 400 (missing name)

docs.title: GET /api/projects
docs.text:
List all projects for the authenticated user.

Response 200: Array of project objects.

docs.title: GET /api/projects/:id
docs.text:
Get a single project with its entry fields.

Response 200: 

{ "id": "...", "name": "...", "status": "ACTIVE", "entryFields": [...] }
Errors: 404 (not found)

docs.title: PUT /api/projects/:id
docs.text:
Update a project's name or description.

Field Type Required name string No description string No

Response 200: Updated project object. Errors: 409 (duplicate name), 404 (not found)

docs.title: PATCH /api/projects/:id/status
docs.text:
Toggle a project between ACTIVE and ARCHIVED.

Field Type Required status string Yes — "ACTIVE" or "ARCHIVED"

Response 200: Updated project object. Errors: 400 (invalid status), 404 (not found)

docs.title: DELETE /api/projects/:id
docs.text:
Permanently delete a project together with its entry fields, entries, their values and version history, and its tag links. Unlike archiving (PATCH /api/projects/:id/status), this can't be undone — the interface asks for the project's name to be typed first.

Response 200: { "message": "Project deleted", "deletedEntries": 12 } Errors: 404 (not found, or not the caller's)

docs.title: GET /api/projects/:id/time-summary
docs.text:
Get aggregated time statistics for a project.

Response 200: 

{ "totalMinutes": 180, "totalHours": 3, "entryCount": 5, "lastEntryAt": "2026-09-14T..." }

docs.title: POST /api/projects/:projectId/entry-fields
docs.text:
Create a custom entry field for a project.

Field Type Required Notes name string Yes type string Yes TEXT, NUMBER, DATE, BOOLEAN, TAGS, CHECKLIST, LINK, REFERENCE, COMPUTED required boolean No Default false. Always stored as false for COMPUTED, which fills itself in formula string COMPUTED only Required for COMPUTED, rejected for every other type. See Computed formulas

Creating a COMPUTED field also fills in its value on the project's existing entries, and every change to a project's fields saves a new format version.

Response 201: Created entry field object. Errors: 400 (missing name, unknown type, missing or invalid formula), 404 (project not found)

docs.title: Computed formulas
docs.text:
A formula is arithmetic over other fields of the same project, referenced by id in braces:

{hours-field-id} * {rate-field-id}
({pay-field-id} + 50) * 1.15
  • Only numbers, + - * /, parentheses and {field-id} references are allowed.
  • A reference must be a NUMBER or another COMPUTED field in the project. Computed fields are always recalculated in dependency order, never read from a previously stored value.
  • A field may not use itself, directly or through a loop of computed fields.
  • A referenced value that an entry left empty counts as 0. A result that is not a finite number (for example, dividing by zero) rejects the entry.
  • The web app lets people write {Field name} and converts names to ids before calling the API. The API itself only accepts ids.

docs.title: Field names are unique within a project
docs.text:
A project cannot have two live fields with the same name. The comparison ignores case and surrounding whitespace, so Hours, hours and Hours are the same name, and both creating and renaming are checked. A field that has been removed is archived rather than deleted, and an archived name is released for reuse.

The rule is enforced by a partial unique index on (project_id, lower(name)) WHERE archived_at IS NULL, not only by the API check — the API check is a read followed by a write and would race under concurrent requests, so two simultaneous creations of the same name resolve to one 201 and one 409 rather than two fields.

Duplicates used to be allowed, and the consequence was not cosmetic. A US22 expression such as SUM({Double hours}) is refused as ambiguous, which made the field unusable in statistics, and a US24 automation rule offered two identically-labelled fields the student could not tell apart.

Errors: 409 (a live field in this project already has that name)

docs.title: GET /api/projects/:projectId/entry-fields
docs.text:
List the project's current entry fields, oldest first. Archived (deleted) fields are left out; they remain in the format version snapshots.

Response 200: Array of entry field objects. Errors: 404 (project not found)

docs.title: GET /api/projects/:projectId/entry-format-versions
docs.text:
List all format version snapshots for a project.

Response 200: Array of format version objects.

docs.title: PUT /api/entry-fields/:id
docs.text:
Update an entry field. All body fields are optional.

Field Type Notes name string Cannot be blank type string Only while no entry has a value for the field required boolean Always false for COMPUTED formula string COMPUTED only; same rules as Computed formulas

When the formula changes, or a field becomes COMPUTED, the stored result is recalculated on every existing entry in the project. So is every computed field that uses this one, directly or indirectly. This happens in the same transaction as the field update, so entries and statistics never mix old and new results. An entry the new formula cannot be worked out for (for example, a division by zero) is left without a value. Renaming a field does not touch stored results.

Response 200: Updated entry field object. Errors: 400 (blank name, unknown type, invalid formula or loop, formula on a non-computed field), 404 (field not found), 409 (type change on a field that already has values)

docs.title: DELETE /api/entry-fields/:id
docs.text:
Soft-delete (archive) an entry field. Existing entries retain their values; the field is hidden from new entry forms.

Response 204: No content. Errors: 404 (field not found)

docs.title: GET /api/entries
docs.text:
List entries across every project belonging to the authenticated user, so a page showing several projects needs one request rather than one per project.

Scoped to the caller: entries are reached by joining through the owning project, so an id belonging to another account returns nothing rather than that account's data.

Query param Type Default Notes projectId string — Restrict to one project. A project the caller does not own yields an empty list, not a 404 projectStatus string ALL ACTIVE, ARCHIVED or ALL from string — ISO date or datetime, inclusive lower bound to string — ISO date or datetime, inclusive upper bound limit number 200 Capped at 500 offset number 0 Rows to skip, for paging ("load more") archived string exclude exclude, only or include archived entries

from and to filter on COALESCE(entryDate, createdAt) — the date the interface shows. An entry backdated to March counts as March, not as the day it was typed, which is what the timeline and calendar already display.

Results are ordered newest first by that same date, with the entry id as a tiebreaker so the order is stable between identical dates.

Response 200:

{
  "entries": [
    {
      "id": "…",
      "projectId": "…",
      "durationMinutes": 45,
      "entryDate": null,
      "dueDate": null,
      "values": { "<fieldId>": "…" },
      "status": "OPEN",
      "completedAt": null,
      "tags": ["coursework"],
      "formatVersionId": "…",
      "createdAt": "…",
      "updatedAt": "…"
    }
  ],
  "formats": {
    "<formatVersionId>": { "version": 3, "fields": [ … ] }
  },
  "limit": 200,
  "offset": 0,
  "truncated": false
}

Unlike GET /api/projects/:projectId/entries, an entry does not carry its own format. Each entry names its formatVersionId and the snapshots are returned once in the shared formats map — a term of entries on a nine-field project would otherwise be mostly repeated schema. An entry predating format versioning has formatVersionId: null.

truncated is true when exactly limit rows were returned, meaning there may be more. To fetch the next page, repeat the request with offset increased by limit.

Errors: 400 for an unknown projectStatus or archived value, a non-positive limit, a negative offset, or an unparseable from/to. 401 when the token is missing or invalid.

docs.title: GET /api/me/open-entries
docs.text:
Every OPEN entry across all of the authenticated user's projects, newest first, in one request. Used by the Open Work page instead of one request per project.

Response 200: an array of entry objects, each with its own format and an added projectName.

Errors: 401

docs.title: POST /api/projects/:projectId/entries
docs.text:
Create a new logbook entry.

Field Type Required Notes durationMinutes number Yes values object Yes Key = field ID, value = field value entryDate string No ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) recurrence object No Creates a recurrence rule: { "pattern": "DAILY" | "WEEKLY" | "MONTHLY", "until"?: ISO date } dueDate string No ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD)

Response 201: Created entry object with status: "OPEN".

When an entry includes recurrence, the original and each generated occurrence expose a recurrence object containing its rule id, pattern, enabled state and next occurrence. Due occurrences are generated automatically while the backend is running and are also caught up when the student's entries are read.

docs.title: PATCH /api/recurrences/:id
docs.text:
Enable or disable future automatic occurrences for a recurring-entry rule. The rule must belong to the authenticated user.

Body field Type Required Description enabled boolean Yes false stops future entries; existing entries remain unchanged.

Response 200: Updated recurrence summary.

docs.title: GET /api/projects/:projectId/entries
docs.text:
List entries for a project. Supports filtering.

Query param Type Notes status string Filter by OPEN or DONE dueBefore string ISO date — returns entries due before this date archived string exclude (default) leaves archived entries out, only returns just the archive, include returns both. Also accepted by GET /api/entries.

Response 200: Array of entry objects. Each has archivedAt (null while active).

docs.title: PUT /api/entries/:id
docs.text:
Update an entry's duration, values, or dates.

Field Type Required durationMinutes number No values object No entryDate string No dueDate string No

Response 200: Updated entry object.

docs.title: PATCH /api/entries/:id/status
docs.text:
Update an entry's status (mark as done or reopen).

Field Type Required status string Yes — "OPEN" or "DONE"

Response 200: 

{ "id": "...", "status": "DONE", "completedAt": "2026-09-14T..." }
Errors: 400 (invalid status), 404 (not found)

docs.title: DELETE /api/entries/:id
docs.text:
Permanently delete an entry and all its values.

Response 200: { "message": "Entry deleted." } Errors: 404 (not found)

docs.title: Entry History & Archive (/api/...) 🔒
docs.text:
Every create, edit, status change and restore of an entry saves a new version — a snapshot of the entry's content at that moment. Versions are never changed or deleted, so an edit can't overwrite what the entry said before. Entries created before this feature existed show their current state as version 1 until their first change.

A version object: 

{
  "version": 2,
  "reason": "UPDATED",
  "restoredFromVersion": null,
  "createdAt": "2026-09-24T10:15:00.000Z",
  "snapshot": { "durationMinutes": 45, "entryDate": null, "dueDate": null, "values": { "<fieldId>": "..." }, "format": { "version": 1, "fields": [] }, "tags": [], "status": "OPEN", "completedAt": null }
}
reason is CREATED, UPDATED or RESTORED.

docs.title: GET /api/entries/:id/versions
docs.text:
The entry's full history, oldest first.

Response 200: { "entryId": "...", "entryCreatedAt": "...", "currentVersion": 3, "versions": [ ...version objects ] } Errors: 404 (not found)

docs.title: GET /api/entries/:id/versions/at?date=<ISO date>
docs.text:
The entry as it stood at a moment in time: the newest version saved at or before date.

Response 200: - { "existed": true, "entryCreatedAt": "...", "version": { ... }, "isCurrent": false } - { "existed": false, "entryCreatedAt": "..." } when date is before the entry was created

Errors: 400 (missing or invalid date), 404 (not found)

docs.title: POST /api/entries/:id/versions/:version/restore
docs.text:
Make an earlier version the current entry. The restore is saved as a new RESTORED version, so the version being replaced stays in the history. Values for fields since deleted from the project can't come back and are counted in skippedFields.

Response 200: { "entry": { ...entry }, "version": { ...the new version }, "skippedFields": 0 } Errors: 400 (invalid version number), 404 (entry or version not found)

docs.title: PATCH /api/entries/:id/archive
docs.text:
Move one entry to the archive, or back to the active logbook.

Field Type Required archived boolean Yes

Response 200: Updated entry object. Errors: 400, 404 (not found)

docs.title: POST /api/entries/archive
docs.text:
Archive (or restore) several selected entries at once. Ids that aren't the caller's are skipped.

Field Type Required ids string[] Yes — 1 to 500 entry ids archived boolean Yes

Response 200: { "updated": 2 } Errors: 400

docs.title: POST /api/projects/:projectId/stats/group
docs.text:
Aggregate entry field values with grouping.

Field Type Required Notes metricFieldId string Yes ID of the field to aggregate operation string Yes sum, avg, min, max or count. All but count need a Number or Computed field groupByFieldId string No ID of the field to group by

Blank and non-numeric values are left out of the calculation rather than failing it.

Response 200: 

{ "groups": [{ "key": "Category A", "value": 195 }] }
Without groupByFieldId, there is one group with key: "total".

Errors: 400 (missing field, bad operation, type mismatch), 404 (project or field not found)

docs.title: POST /api/projects/:projectId/stats/timeline
docs.text:
Plot entries over time: how many fall in each bucket, or the total of a numeric field per bucket.

Field Type Required Notes dateFieldId string Yes ID of a DATE-type field bucket string No day (default), week, or month operation string No count (default) or sum metricFieldId string For sum A Number or Computed field to total

Response 200: 

{ "points": [{ "date": "2026-09-01", "value": 5 }, { "date": "2026-09-02", "value": 3 }] }
Errors: 400 (invalid bucket or operation, non-DATE field, missing field), 404 (project or field not found)

docs.title: POST /api/projects/:projectId/stats/expression
docs.text:
Evaluate a custom expression (US22) across every entry in the project, and return the single number it works out to.

Field Type Required Notes expression string Yes Up to 500 characters

Syntax. COUNT() counts the entries in the project. SUM(field), AVG(field), MIN(field) and MAX(field) aggregate one Number or Computed field. These combine with +, -, *, / and parentheses, with the usual precedence. A field is named directly (SUM(hours)), or in braces when the name contains spaces (SUM({Tasks Completed})). Names are matched without regard to capitals.

Request: 

{ "expression": "SUM({Hours}) / COUNT()" }

Response 200: 

{ "value": 3.42 }

Semantics. Values that are not readable as a number are skipped, so AVG averages the values it can read rather than dividing by the entry count. A field no entry has filled in sums to 0; averaging, minimising or maximising it is an error rather than a misleading zero. Computed fields aggregate like any other number, using the value already stored per entry — the formula is not re-evaluated here.

Errors: 400 (empty or malformed expression, unknown function, unknown or duplicated field name, non-numeric field, unbalanced parentheses, division by zero), 401 (not signed in), 404 (project not found, which is also what another owner's project returns)

Expressions are parsed and evaluated by the server; no user input is ever executed, and field names reach the database only as bound parameters after being matched against the project's own fields.

docs.title: Custom Statistics (/api/projects/:projectId/custom-statistics) 🔒
docs.text:
US23. A saved custom expression with a name, kept alongside the built-in statistics and available as a dashboard panel. Only the definition is stored: every read works the value out from the project's current entries, so a saved statistic follows the data instead of freezing the number it had when saved.

A statistic object: 

{ "id": "...", "projectId": "...", "name": "Average hours", "expression": "AVG({Hours})", "value": 3.42, "error": null, "createdAt": "...", "updatedAt": "..." }
If a statistic can no longer be worked out (for example, its field was renamed or deleted), value is null and error says why, instead of the whole request failing.

Names and expressions are trimmed. A name is up to 100 characters and unique within the project; an expression is up to 500 characters and uses the expression syntax.

docs.title: POST /api/projects/:projectId/custom-statistics
docs.text:
Save a statistic. The expression is checked against the project's fields but does not need any entries yet.

Field Type Required name string Yes expression string Yes

Response 201: the statistic object. Errors: 400 (empty name or expression, invalid expression), 404 (project not found), 409 (name already used in this project)

docs.title: GET /api/projects/:projectId/custom-statistics
docs.text:
The project's statistics, oldest first, each with its current value.

Response 200: an array of statistic objects.

docs.title: GET /api/projects/:projectId/custom-statistics/:id
docs.text:
One statistic with its current value.

Response 200: the statistic object. Errors: 404 (project or statistic not found)

docs.title: PATCH /api/projects/:projectId/custom-statistics/:id
docs.text:
Rename a statistic or change its expression. At least one must be given.

Field Type Required name string No expression string No

Response 200: the updated statistic object. Errors: 400, 404, 409 (as for create)

docs.title: DELETE /api/projects/:projectId/custom-statistics/:id
docs.text: Response 200: { "message": "Statistic deleted" } Errors: 404 (project or statistic not found)

docs.title: Tags (/api/tags) 🔒
docs.text: Each user has their own tag vocabulary, shared by their projects and entries. Tags are created implicitly: sending a new tag name on a project or entry adds it. These endpoints read and prune that vocabulary.

docs.title: GET /api/tags
docs.text:
List the authenticated user's tags, alphabetically.

Response 200: 

[{ "id": "...", "name": "coursework" }, { "id": "...", "name": "urgent" }]

docs.title: DELETE /api/tags/:id
docs.text:
Delete a tag from the vocabulary. It is removed from every project and entry it was on; the projects and entries themselves are not changed otherwise.

Response 204: No content. Errors: 404 (tag not found, or not the caller's)

docs.title: Reminders (/api/reminders) 🔒
docs.text:
US28. A reminder is either set by hand (source: "MANUAL") or generated from the user's reminder rules:

Source Generated when DUE_SOON An open, unarchived entry's due date is within dueSoonDays days OVERDUE An open, unarchived entry's due date has passed STALE An open, unarchived entry has not been edited for staleDays days DAILY_LOG Nothing has been logged today and it is past dailyLogTime

Rules are evaluated whenever reminders are read (GET /reminders and GET /reminders/count). Each condition produces at most one reminder, so a completed or dismissed reminder stays that way while the condition holds. A pending generated reminder whose condition lapses is marked COMPLETED if its entry was marked done (or, for DAILY_LOG, something was logged), and removed otherwise, e.g. when the due date moves or the rule is switched off. Calendar days are counted in the rules' timeZone.

Reminder object: 

{
  "id": "...",
  "title": "Due soon: Submit lab report",
  "note": null,
  "source": "DUE_SOON",
  "status": "PENDING",
  "remindAt": "2026-09-26T10:00:00.000Z",
  "completedAt": null,
  "dismissedAt": null,
  "createdAt": "2026-09-26T10:00:00.000Z",
  "entry": {
    "id": "...", "projectId": "...", "projectName": "Chemistry",
    "label": "Submit lab report", "dueDate": "2026-09-27T00:00:00.000Z", "status": "OPEN"
  }
}

docs.title: GET /api/reminders
docs.text:
List the caller's reminders.

Query: status = pending (default) | completed | dismissed | done (completed + dismissed) | all; due=true keeps only reminders whose remindAt has passed. Pending reminders are ordered by remindAt; others most recently changed first. At most 200.

Response 200: array of reminder objects. Errors: 400 (unknown status)

docs.title: GET /api/reminders/count
docs.text: Response 200: { "due": 3 }: pending reminders whose time has come.

docs.title: POST /api/reminders
docs.text:
Set a reminder by hand.

Body: 

{ "title": "Email supervisor", "remindAt": "2026-09-27T09:00:00.000Z", "note": "optional", "entryId": "optional uuid" }

Response 201: the reminder. Errors: 400 (missing title, invalid date), 404 (entry not found, or not the caller's)

docs.title: PATCH /api/reminders/:id
docs.text:
Complete, dismiss, reopen, snooze or edit a reminder. Send any of status (PENDING | COMPLETED | DISMISSED), title, note, remindAt. Setting a status stamps completedAt/dismissedAt; PENDING clears both.

Response 200: the reminder. Errors: 400 (invalid value, empty body), 404

docs.title: DELETE /api/reminders/:id
docs.text:
Delete a manual reminder. Generated reminders would come back while their condition holds, so they must be dismissed instead.

Response 204: No content. Errors: 400 (generated reminder), 404

docs.title: GET /api/reminders/settings
docs.text:
The caller's reminder rules (defaults shown): 

{
  "dueSoonEnabled": true, "dueSoonDays": 1,
  "overdueEnabled": true,
  "staleEnabled": false, "staleDays": 7,
  "dailyLogEnabled": false, "dailyLogTime": "18:00",
  "timeZone": "UTC"
}

docs.title: PUT /api/reminders/settings
docs.text:
Update any subset of the rules. dueSoonDays 0–30, staleDays 1–365, dailyLogTime HH:MM, timeZone an IANA zone name.

Response 200: the full rules. Errors: 400 (out-of-range or invalid value)

docs.title: Dashboard layout (/api/dashboard) 🔒
docs.text: US25/US26. The panels on the caller's dashboard, in the order they arranged them, saved to their account so the layout is the same on every device. A built-in panel is named by its id ("activity", "recent-entries", …). A saved statistic (US23) is "stat:<projectId>:<statisticId>", and the dashboard reads its value from GET /projects/:projectId/custom-statistics/:id. The frontend skips ids it doesn't know, so the server only checks their format.

docs.title: GET /api/dashboard/layout
docs.text: Response 200: { "panels": ["tags", "stat:<uuid>:<uuid>"], "updatedAt": "..." }, or { "panels": null, "updatedAt": null } when the caller has never saved one (the default dashboard). An empty array is a saved, empty dashboard.

docs.title: PUT /api/dashboard/layout
docs.text:
Replace the saved layout. Body: { "panels": ["recent-entries", "activity"] } (at most 50, each once).

Response 200: the saved layout. Errors: 400 (not an array, unknown id format, duplicates, too many)

docs.title: DELETE /api/dashboard/layout
docs.text: Go back to the default dashboard. Response 204: No content.

docs.title: Push notifications (/api/push) 🔒
docs.text:
Web push for reminders. When VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY and VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY are set, a job runs every minute. For each user with a subscribed device, it applies their reminder rules and pushes every pending reminder whose remindAt has passed and that hasn't been pushed yet. If more than three are due at once, it sends one summary instead. Snoozing a reminder (a new remindAt) lets it be pushed again. Without the keys, push is off and reminders stay in-app only.

Push payload, as the service worker receives it: 

{ "title": "Due soon: Submit lab report", "body": "Chemistry: Submit lab report", "url": "/reminders", "tag": "reminder-<id>" }

docs.title: GET /api/push/public-key
docs.text: Response 200: { "publicKey": "B..." }, or { "publicKey": null } when push is off.

docs.title: POST /api/push/subscriptions
docs.text:
Register this device. The body is the browser's PushSubscription.toJSON(). Reminders already due at this point count as pushed, so a new device isn't sent old ones. Re-sending an endpoint updates it, and moves it to the caller if another user had it.

Body: 

{ "endpoint": "https://fcm.googleapis.com/...", "keys": { "p256dh": "...", "auth": "..." } }

Response 201: { "subscribed": true } Errors: 400 (malformed subscription), 503 (push not set up on the server)

docs.title: DELETE /api/push/subscriptions
docs.text:
Stop pushing to a device. Body: { "endpoint": "..." }

Response 204: No content. Devices the push service reports as gone (404/410) are removed automatically.

docs.title: Automation Rules (/api/projects/:projectId/automation-rules) 🔒
docs.text:
US24. An automation rule watches one project's entries and applies an action when its conditions hold. Rules run automatically when an entry is saved — after POST .../entries, PUT /api/entries/:id and PATCH /api/entries/:id/status — once the save has committed. Automation never fails a save: a broken rule is logged and skipped, and the user's work always survives.

Rule object: 

{
  "id": "...",
  "projectId": "...",
  "name": "Long session",
  "trigger": "ENTRY_CREATED",
  "conditions": [
    { "source": "ATTRIBUTE", "attribute": "durationMinutes", "operator": "GTE", "value": 240 }
  ],
  "action": { "type": "ADD_TAG", "tagId": "..." },
  "enabled": true,
  "invalidReason": null,
  "createdAt": "2026-09-27T10:00:00.000Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-09-27T10:00:00.000Z"
}

invalidReason is null while the rule can run. A rule can go stale after it is written — its field archived, its tag deleted — and then carries a human- readable reason instead; the runner refuses to act on exactly these rules, so a stale rule is inert rather than misfiring.

docs.title: POST /api/projects/:projectId/automation-rules
docs.text:
Create a rule. name (≤100 chars, unique per project), trigger (ENTRY_CREATED | ENTRY_UPDATED), conditions (1–10, ANDed), action, enabled (optional, default true). See Semantics and deliberate limitations for the condition and action shapes.

Response 201: the rule. Errors: 400 (malformed rule, or a fieldId/tagId that does not belong to this project or its owner), 404 (project not found, or not the caller's), 409 (duplicate name)

docs.title: GET /api/projects/:projectId/automation-rules
docs.text:
List the project's rules in execution order (oldest first, tie-broken by id) — the same order the runner applies them.

Response 200: array of rules.

docs.title: GET /api/projects/:projectId/automation-rules/:id
docs.text: Response 200: the rule. Errors: 404 (rule not found, or not the caller's)

docs.title: PATCH /api/projects/:projectId/automation-rules/:id
docs.text:
Change any subset of name, trigger, conditions, action, enabled. When conditions or action are supplied, the rule is validated as it will be after the edit — swapping only the action can invalidate conditions that were fine, and vice versa.

Response 200: the updated rule. Errors: 400 (malformed or invalid rule), 404 (rule not found, or not the caller's), 409 (duplicate name)

docs.title: DELETE /api/projects/:projectId/automation-rules/:id
docs.text: Response 200: { "message": "Rule deleted" } Errors: 404 (rule not found, or not the caller's)

docs.title: Semantics and deliberate limitations
docs.text:
Triggers. ENTRY_CREATED fires on entry creation; ENTRY_UPDATED fires on every later save, including a status-only change through PATCH /entries/:id/status — so "when an entry is marked done" works no matter which endpoint the UI reaches for.

Conditions are a flat AND list over either an entry attribute (durationMinutes, status) or a project field (fieldId). Comparison operators: EQ, NEQ, GT, GTE, LT, LTE; presence/truth operators: IS_EMPTY, IS_NOT_EMPTY, IS_TRUE, IS_FALSE. Which operators apply is gated by what the condition reads — NUMBER/COMPUTED fields get the comparisons, TEXT/LINK get equality and presence, BOOLEAN gets IS_TRUE/IS_FALSE. DATE, TAGS, CHECKLIST and REFERENCE fields cannot be used in conditions at all: a stored EntryValue holds whatever string passed Date.parse, so two dates meaning the same day could compare unequal, and the story needs no date rules. Numeric parsing follows the same strictness as statistics: "12kg" is not 12, a blank is not 0, and a value that cannot be parsed makes the comparison false rather than coercing it.

Actions are ADD_TAG, REMOVE_TAG and SET_STATUS only. There is deliberately no action that writes a field value (it would collide with COMPUTED fields and required-field validation), none that sets a date, and none that creates entries — that last would let one rule spawn unbounded entries and would interact badly with offline replay. SET_STATUS maintains completedAt exactly as a manual status change does.

Ordering and idempotency. Rules run oldest-first; when several rules set the status, the last one wins. Every action is idempotent — ADD_TAG inserts against the entry-tag composite key, REMOVE_TAG is a delete, SET_STATUS skips a no-op write — so the offline queue replaying a capture cannot double-apply a rule.

No cascades. Each pass evaluates every rule against one snapshot taken before any action runs, and actions write directly rather than re-entering the save handlers, so a rule's action cannot feed another rule's condition — within the same pass or a later one.

History. toSnapshot() covers tags and status, so what automation did is recorded as a further entry version: the user's save is version n, automation's effect is n+1, visible and revertable in the history UI.

docs.title: Google Calendar (/api/google-calendar)
docs.text:
Syncs open entries' due dates into the user's primary Google Calendar using the Google Calendar API (OAuth 2.0, scope calendar.events). Each open entry with a due date becomes an all-day event. The logbook tags its events with private extended properties, so a sync can find them again: it creates new events, updates events whose date or title changed, and removes events for entries that were completed, undated, or deleted. Events the user created themselves are never touched.

Google access and refresh tokens are stored per user, encrypted with AES-256-GCM (GOOGLE_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY). They are never returned by the API.

docs.title: GET /api/google-calendar/connect 🔒
docs.text:
Returns the Google consent URL. The URL carries a signed, 10-minute state token bound to the caller, which the callback requires.

Response 200: 

{ "url": "https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth?...&state=..." }
Errors: 500 (Google Calendar not configured on the server)

docs.title: GET /api/google-calendar/callback
docs.text:
Google redirects the browser here after consent. It is not called by the SPA. The user is identified only from the signed state. On completion the browser is redirected to APP_URL/calendar?calendar=connected, =denied (the user cancelled), or =error.

Query Notes code Authorization code from Google state Signed state issued by /connect

Errors: 400 (missing code or state), 401 (invalid or expired state)

docs.title: GET /api/google-calendar/status 🔒
docs.text:
Response 200: 

{ "configured": true, "connected": true, "connectedAt": "2026-09-24T10:00:00.000Z" }

docs.title: POST /api/google-calendar/sync 🔒
docs.text:
Mirrors the caller's open, dated entries into Google Calendar. Safe to repeat.

Response 200: 

{ "message": "Due dates synced to Google Calendar.", "created": 2, "updated": 1, "removed": 0 }
Errors: 400 (not connected), 409 (access was revoked in the Google account; the connection is removed and the user must reconnect), 502 (Google API failure)

docs.title: DELETE /api/google-calendar/disconnect 🔒
docs.text:
Revokes the grant at Google (best effort) and deletes the stored tokens. Events that were already synced remain in the user's calendar.

Response 200: 

{ "message": "Google Calendar connection removed." }

docs.title: Error Format
docs.text:
All error responses use a consistent JSON shape:

{ "error": "Human-readable error message" }
Status Meaning 400 Validation error (bad input, missing field, invalid enum) 401 Authentication failure (missing or invalid JWT, wrong password) 403 Forbidden (e.g. unverified account trying to log in) 404 Resource not found — also returned for a resource that belongs to another user, so its existence is not revealed 409 Conflict (duplicate name or email) 429 Too many requests — the rate limit on sign-in, sign-up or 2FA was hit; wait and try again 500 Unexpected server error 503 A feature is not configured on this server (the 2FA encryption key or the push keys)

Request bodies that fail Zod validation on the auth routes return { "errors": { "<field>": ["message"] } } instead of a single error string.

docs.title: External Integrations
docs.text:
Service Purpose Configuration Neon Hosted PostgreSQL database DATABASE_URL in .env Google Calendar API Syncs entry due dates to the user's calendar (details) GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI, GOOGLE_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY, APP_URL Resend Transactional email (preferred) RESEND_API_KEY in .env Gmail SMTP Transactional email (fallback) GMAIL_USER + GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD in .env Web push Reminder notifications to subscribed devices (details) VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY, VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY, optional VAPID_SUBJECT

When neither email provider is configured, the backend runs in dev mode: registration auto-verifies and password-reset emails are logged to the console instead of sent.

🔒 = requires Authorization: Bearer <token> header.

Related: Authentication & Security Guide covers the 2FA lifecycle, password reset flow, and security properties in detail. Testing documents the automated test coverage for every endpoint listed above.

docs.title: System Architecture
docs.text: The Digital Logbook is a single-page React application talking to an Express REST API, backed by PostgreSQL. Frontend, backend and a shared types package live in one npm-workspaces monorepo.

docs.title: 1. Deployment Overview
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    Browser["Browser<br/>React SPA + service worker"]
    Pages["Cloudflare Pages<br/>static frontend build"]
    API["Render<br/>Express API + background jobs"]
    DB[("Neon<br/>PostgreSQL")]
    Push["Browser push service<br/>(web push)"]
    Google["Google Calendar API"]
    Mail["Resend / Gmail SMTP"]

    Browser -- "loads app" --> Pages
    Browser -- "HTTPS /api, JWT" --> API
    API -- "Prisma over pg" --> DB
    API -- "VAPID-signed pushes" --> Push
    Push -- "notifications" --> Browser
    API -- "OAuth, event sync" --> Google
    API -- "verification & reset emails" --> Mail
Part Hosted on Notes Frontend Cloudflare Pages (*.pages.dev) Static Vite build. A production build calls the Render API directly; the dev server proxies /api to localhost:3000 instead. Backend Render One Node process serving the API and running the background jobs (§6). On the free tier it sleeps when idle, and the jobs pause with it. Database Neon (serverless PostgreSQL) Reached through Prisma's pg driver adapter. CI Gitea Actions (.gitea/workflows/deploy.yaml) Installs, typechecks, lints, tests and builds on every push. It deploys nothing; both deployments are done by hand.

The backend only accepts browser requests from localhost and *.pages.dev origins (CORS, apps/backend/src/app.ts).

docs.title: 4. Data Model
docs.text:
The schema in apps/backend/prisma/schema.prisma has twenty models. See Database design for the full diagram; they group as follows.

Area Models Notes Accounts User, PasswordReset, TwoFactorRecoveryCode Reset and verification tokens are stored hashed. TOTP secrets are encrypted at rest. Projects & formats Project, EntryField, EntryFormatVersion A project's entry format is its fields. Each format change writes an immutable EntryFormatVersion, and an entry stays pinned to the version it was created under. Entries LogbookEntry, EntryValue One EntryValue row per field per entry, stored as text and interpreted by the field's type. Entries carry duration, entry and due dates, an OPEN/DONE status, and an archivedAt marker. History EntryVersion A full snapshot of the entry on every create, edit, restore and automated change. Rows are never updated. Tags Tag, ProjectTag, EntryTag User-scoped labels for projects and entries. Statistics & dashboard CustomStatistic, DashboardLayout Saved expressions, and the user's chosen dashboard panels in order. Automation AutomationRule, RecurrenceRule Rules applied when entries are saved, and templates for repeating entries. Reminders Reminder, ReminderSettings, PushSubscription Manual and rule-generated reminders, each user's rules, and the devices subscribed to push. Integrations GoogleCalendarConnection Encrypted OAuth tokens for Calendar sync.

Field types (EntryFieldType): TEXT, NUMBER, DATE, BOOLEAN, TAGS, CHECKLIST, LINK, REFERENCE, COMPUTED.

Key constraints: one account per email; project names unique per user; field names unique per project (case-insensitive, among non-archived fields); one value per field per entry; version numbers unique per entry. Foreign keys cascade on delete, so deleting an account erases all of its data.

docs.title: 5. API
docs.text:
All routes are under /api and, apart from sign-up, sign-in, password reset and the health checks, need a Bearer JWT. Every request body is validated with Zod (400 on failure), and every resource is checked against the signed-in user (404 for another user's data). The full list with request and response shapes is in the API Reference.

Area Base paths Authentication, 2FA, account /auth/* Projects /projects, /projects/:id, /projects/:id/time-summary, /projects/:id/status Entry fields & formats /projects/:projectId/entry-fields, /projects/:projectId/entry-format-versions, /entry-fields/:id Entries /entries, /projects/:projectId/entries, /entries/:id, /entries/:id/status, /me/open-entries History & archive /entries/:id/versions, /entries/:id/versions/at, /entries/:id/versions/:version/restore, /entries/archive, /entries/:id/archive Statistics /projects/:projectId/stats/{group,timeline,expression}, /projects/:projectId/custom-statistics Automation /projects/:projectId/automation-rules, /recurrences/:id Reminders & push /reminders, /reminders/count, /reminders/settings, /push/public-key, /push/subscriptions Dashboard /dashboard/layout Tags /tags Google Calendar /google-calendar/{connect,callback,status,sync,disconnect} Utility /health, /db-check

docs.title: Saving an entry
docs.text:
Creating or editing an entry (entry.controller.ts) happens in this order:

  1. The request is validated, each value is checked against its field's type, computed fields are calculated from the supplied values, and required fields are checked.
  2. In one database transaction, the entry and its values are written and an EntryVersion snapshot is recorded.
  3. After the transaction commits, matching automation rules run (utils/automationRunner.ts). They can add or remove tags or set the status, and record their change as a further version. Rules cannot trigger themselves or each other, and a failing rule is skipped. Running them after the commit means a broken rule can never cost the user their entry.

Because every save writes a version, the history, "as of a date" view and restore features all read from the same EntryVersion rows.

docs.title: Background jobs
docs.text:
src/index.ts starts three jobs with the server:

Job Interval Does recurringEntries every minute Creates entries whose recurrence rule has fallen due pushReminders every minute Generates each subscribed user's reminders from their rules and pushes the ones now due. Off when the VAPID keys are not set. purgeDeletedAccounts every hour Permanently deletes accounts whose 30-day deletion grace period has ended

The jobs run only while the server is awake. The work is also done on demand: listing entries creates any due recurring entries, and reading reminders generates them, so nothing is lost while the server sleeps. Only push notifications wait until it wakes.

docs.title: Reminders and notifications
docs.text:
Reminders come from the user (MANUAL) or from their rules (DUE_SOON, OVERDUE, STALE, DAILY_LOG). A device can be notified in two ways:

  • Push: where the browser supports it and the server has VAPID keys, the browser subscribes and the server pushes each reminder as it falls due, even with the logbook closed. public/sw.js receives the push and shows it.
  • In-app: otherwise, an open logbook tab checks for newly due reminders every five minutes and shows them itself.

The service worker is registered only in production builds, so local development always uses the in-app path.

docs.title: Offline use
docs.text: The service worker caches the app shell, so the logbook opens with no connection. API data is cached separately by the app (lib/offlineCache.ts), and entries created offline are queued (lib/offlineEntries.ts) and sent when the connection returns.

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text: A successful sign-in returns a JWT that lasts seven days, kept in localStorage. The Axios client attaches it to every request. A 401 from any route other than the credential checks clears the session and returns the user to /login?expired=1.

docs.title: 7. Frontend Structure
docs.text:
App (BrowserRouter)
├── Public routes
│   ├── /                  LandingPage
│   ├── /login             LoginPage (with 2FA and recovery codes)
│   ├── /register          RegisterPage
│   ├── /verify-email      VerifyEmail
│   ├── /forgot-password   ForgotPasswordPage
│   └── /reset-password    ResetPasswordPage
│
└── Protected routes (ProtectedRoute → AppLayout with Sidebar)
    ├── /dashboard         DashboardPage: chosen and arranged panels, including saved statistics
    ├── /projects          ProjectsPage: projects and their entry formats
    ├── /projects/:id      ProjectDetailPage: entries, format, automation rules
    ├── /entries           EntriesPage: all entries, search, filters, saved filters, archive
    ├── /stats             StatsPage: group-by, timeline, custom expressions, saved statistics
    ├── /open-work         OpenWorkPage: unfinished entries by urgency
    ├── /calendar          CalendarPage: entries by due date, Google Calendar sync
    ├── /board             BoardPage: entries as a board
    ├── /reminders         RemindersPage: reminders and reminder rules
    ├── /settings          SettingsPage: account, 2FA, notifications, data export/import
    └── /profile           ProfilePage

Notable components beyond the basic layout, card and state components:

Component Purpose EntryForm, ChecklistInput, TagInput, Stopwatch Entry capture for all nine field types, with a live timer EntryHistoryModal Version history, "as of a date" view and restore AutomationRules Create, edit, enable and delete a project's rules DeadlineReminders Upcoming and overdue due dates GoogleCalendarSync Connect, sync and disconnect Google Calendar BarChart, TrendChart, WeekComparison Statistics and dashboard charts DeleteProjectModal Confirmed project deletion

api/client.ts points the Axios instance at /api in development and at the Render URL in production. api.ts wraps every endpoint in a typed function.

docs.title: 8. Shared Types Package
docs.text: @logbook/shared (packages/shared/src/) exports the types and Zod schemas both apps use, such as projects, entry fields, entries, time summaries, their create and update inputs, and the auth schemas (registerSchema, loginSchema and so on). The backend imports its compiled dist/, so the package must be built after changes. The frontend reads the source directly through a Vite alias.

docs.title: 9. Security
docs.text:
• Passwords are hashed with bcrypt. Password-reset and email-verification tokens are stored only as hashes.
  • TOTP secrets and Google tokens are encrypted at rest with keys from the environment. 2FA has single-use recovery codes, and its second step requires a short-lived token from a successful password check.
  • Sign-in, sign-up and 2FA routes are rate limited per IP.
  • In production the server refuses to start without JWT_SECRET.
  • Every entry, project, statistic, rule and reminder query is scoped to the signed-in user.

docs.title: 10. Testing
docs.text: Both apps use Vitest. The backend suite (apps/backend/src/__tests__/) runs Supertest integration tests against the database in .env, alongside unit tests for pure logic such as expressions and automation conditions. The frontend suite tests components, pages and libraries in jsdom with the API mocked. See Testing for the strategy and Setup for how to run them.

docs.title: Client Interaction Logs
docs.text: This document tracks requirements, Q&A, and decisions made in consultation with the client (lecturers/TAs). It serves as project methodology evidence and records how client feedback influenced the development of the Digital Logbook.

docs.title: [Date: 2026-08-13] — Project Process & Evidence Feedback
docs.text:
• Channel: In-class rubric review.

  • Feedback:

  • Google Form is not sufficient evidence for client interactions; the team must provide documented logs.

  • The team must document its Kanban project methodology.

  • All supporting features must be functional in vertical slices.

  • Action Taken:

  • Adopted the Gitea Kanban board as the project work-tracking system.

  • Created client interaction documentation.
  • Established an issue-to-branch workflow.
  • Continued developing functionality as vertical slices across the database, API, and frontend.

docs.title: [Date: 2026-08-17] — Requirements Clarification Meeting
docs.text:
• Channel: Requirements Review Meeting.

  • Attendees: Client / Lecturer, Development Team (all members).

docs.title: 1. Project Ownership & Naming
docs.text:
• Client Decision: A project is strictly owned by a single student. Project names must be unique for each student (e.g., a student cannot have two projects named "CS Lab 1").

  • Impact:

  • projects table uses user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE.

  • Unique constraint: UNIQUE(user_id, name).

docs.title: 2. Project Archiving Behavior (US05)
docs.text:
• Client Decision: Archiving a project does not lock it into a read-only state. Users can still create new entries, edit/delete existing entries, and unarchive the project at any time.

  • Impact: Archiving is implemented as a UI/filtering state (status = 'ARCHIVED') rather than a backend permission lock. This is handled through PATCH /api/projects/:id/status.

docs.title: 3. Time Tracking, Live Timer & Overdue Flagging (US04)
docs.text:
• Client Decision:

  • Time tracking on logbook entries is mandatory.

  • The system must include a live timer feature for recording entry duration.

  • Entries/tasks must support flagging items as overdue.

  • Impact:

  • logbook_entries requires duration_minutes INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.

  • logbook_entries includes due_date TIMESTAMP to support overdue calculations.
  • logbook_entries includes entry_date TIMESTAMP to support backdating.
  • The frontend requires a live stopwatch/timer widget that calculates elapsed time.

docs.title: 4. Entry Editing & Account Erasure
docs.text:
• Client Decision: Logbook entries can be edited and deleted after creation. When an account is deleted, all user data, projects, and entries must be permanently erased.

  • Impact: Foreign keys enforce ON DELETE CASCADE where appropriate. This behaviour was verified in the Prisma schema.

docs.title: 5. Stats, Analytics & External API Integration
docs.text:
• Client Decision:

  • The system must include project statistics and analytics.

  • The external API integration should use a Calendar API, such as syncing logbook deadlines or entries to an external calendar.

  • Impact:

  • Backend provides GET /api/projects/:id/time-summary for per-project time aggregates.

  • The Dashboard provides cross-project statistics.
  • Calendar integration was identified as a future development requirement.

docs.title: 6. Entry Timestamps & Backdating
docs.text:
• Client Decision: The handling of entry timestamps was left to engineering discretion.

  • Engineering Decision: Include both created_at (system audit timestamp) and entry_date (user-customisable timestamp) on entries. This allows students to backdate work while maintaining an audit record.

docs.title: [Date: 2026-08-21] — Sprint Review & Rubric Compliance Check
docs.text:
• Channel: In-person sprint review meeting with client/lecturer.

  • Attendees: Client / Lecturer, Development Team (Dineo Motloung, Athandwa, Alondwe and Wendy).

docs.title: Meeting Context
docs.text: The client conducted a review of the project against the assessment rubric, checking the implementation status of the required features. The team presented the current state of the application, including authentication, project management, entry CRUD, time tracking, dashboard, profile, and settings.

docs.title: 1. Authentication — Confirmed as Core Requirement
docs.text:
• Discussion: The client confirmed that authentication, including user registration, login, email verification, and password reset, is an explicit rubric requirement and must not be treated as optional or deferred.

  • Status: Fully implemented — JWT-based authentication with registration, login, email verification, password reset, and account deletion.

  • Client Feedback: The client was satisfied with the implementation. Temporary development-mode auto-verification was considered acceptable during development, but production deployment should enforce real email verification.

docs.title: 2. Due Dates & Overdue Flagging — Non-Negotiable
docs.text:
• Discussion: The client reconfirmed that due dates and overdue flagging are mandatory requirements.

  • Decisions:

  • Every logbook entry must support a due_date field.

  • Entries past their due date must be automatically identified as overdue.
  • The UI must provide an Overdue section/filter alongside other entry views.

  • Overdue entries must be visually distinguished.

  • Impact:

  • logbook_entries.due_date is included in the Prisma schema.

  • Overdue status is determined using the entry due date and completion status.
  • The Entries and Project Detail views support overdue filtering.
  • The Dashboard includes overdue information.

docs.title: 3. Live Timer / Stopwatch for Time Tracking
docs.text:
• Discussion: The client emphasised that time tracking should go beyond manually entering a duration. A live stopwatch feature was identified as a required improvement.

  • Decisions:

  • The entry creation/edit form should include a live stopwatch.

  • The stopwatch should support start, pause, and reset.
  • The timer should measure elapsed time and convert it to the required duration value when saved.

  • Users should still be able to enter a duration manually.

  • Impact:

  • A stopwatch component was developed for the entry form.

  • Timer state is persisted during the active session to reduce the risk of losing timing information.
  • The existing duration_minutes backend field supports the saved duration.

docs.title: 4. Overdue Reminders & Notifications
docs.text:
• Discussion: The client asked about reminder capabilities for approaching deadlines.

  • Decisions:

  • The system should support advance reminders, such as reminders three days before, one day before, and on the due date.

  • In-app notifications are sufficient for the current implementation.

  • Email notifications are not required for the initial implementation.

  • Impact:

  • Deadline reminders were implemented in the application.

  • A notification indicator was added to provide users with visibility of notifications.
  • The existing due-date information is used to determine when reminders should be displayed.

docs.title: 5. Calendar API Integration (External API)
docs.text:
• Discussion: The client reconfirmed the requirement for an external API integration. The team proposed Calendar API synchronisation as the most natural integration for a digital logbook.

  • Decisions:

  • Logbook due dates should be exportable or synchronisable to an external calendar.

  • Google Calendar was identified as the preferred integration.

  • Calendar synchronisation was planned for a later development phase.

  • Impact:

  • The existing due_date field provides the required data for calendar events.

  • Google Calendar API integration requires OAuth2 configuration and external service credentials.
  • This feature remains planned for future development.

docs.title: 6. Per-Project Time Recording with Stopwatch
docs.text:
• Discussion: The client asked about recording the total amount of time spent on individual projects.

  • Decisions:

  • Per-project total time should be calculated from the durations of the project's entries.

  • Time recorded using the stopwatch contributes to the relevant entry duration.

  • Project totals should be clearly visible to users.

  • Impact:

  • The existing GET /api/projects/:id/time-summary endpoint provides project-level time aggregation.

  • The Project Detail page can use this information to display cumulative project time.

docs.title: 7. Rubric Compliance Check
docs.text:
The client reviewed the following rubric areas:

  • Authentication & user management — Implemented (registration, login, email verification, password reset, and account deletion).
  • Project CRUD — Implemented (create, read, update, archive/unarchive, and unique name enforcement).
  • Customisable entry formats — Implemented with project-specific field definitions.
  • Entry CRUD with time tracking — Implemented with duration and due-date support.
  • Dashboard & statistics — Implemented with statistics and time summaries.
  • Data export/import — Implemented in Settings.
  • Dark mode / theme — Implemented with light, dark, and system themes.
  • Development setup guide — Implemented and maintained.
  • Testing — Integration tests implemented and passing.
  • Methodology documentation — Kanban board, user stories, and retrospective documentation maintained.

docs.title: [Date: August–September 2026] — Intermediate Development Follow-Up
docs.text:
The Intermediate phase involved significantly fewer formal client interactions than Sprint 1.

Most of the requirements for the Intermediate functionality had already been clarified during the previous in-person client/lecturer meetings, particularly the requirements discussed during the Sprint 1 review. Therefore, the team was able to continue implementation using the confirmed requirements without requiring another formal requirements meeting.

docs.title: Communication Channel
docs.text: • Channel: Team WhatsApp group used for occasional follow-up questions and clarification.

docs.title: Nature of Interaction
docs.text:
During the Intermediate phase, the team used the WhatsApp group to ask a small number of clarification questions when implementation details were unclear.

These interactions were primarily used to confirm interpretation of previously discussed requirements rather than introduce major new requirements.

The team therefore did not hold a separate formal client requirements meeting during this phase.

docs.title: Development Approach
docs.text:
The Intermediate user stories were implemented based on the requirements already established during the previous client meetings:

  • US07–US10: Rich field types, editable entry formats, format version preservation, and computed fields.
  • US11–US13: Custom-field statistics, alternative views, and unfinished-work/due-date functionality.
  • US14–US15: Offline capture, synchronisation, and data export/import.
  • Integration & Testing: Integration of the new functionality with the existing Basic features.

The team maintained the previously agreed Kanban methodology and continued using Gitea Issues, Projects, Labels, and Pull Requests to track implementation.

docs.title: 4. Intermediate Phase Outcomes
docs.text:
The Intermediate functionality was completed and integrated with the existing Basic Digital Logbook functionality.

The completed Intermediate functionality includes:

  • Richer custom field types.
  • Modification of existing entry formats.
  • Preservation of previous entry-format versions.
  • Computed fields.
  • Statistics and analysis of custom fields.
  • Alternative ways of viewing entries.
  • Unfinished-work and due-date tracking.
  • Offline entry capture and synchronisation.
  • Data export and import.

The implementation was tested together with the existing Sprint 1 functionality to identify cross-feature issues and regression problems.

docs.title: 5. Documentation & Deployment Update
docs.text:
During the Intermediate phase, the project documentation was also prepared for online access.

The MkDocs documentation site was successfully deployed using Netlify. The deployed documentation provides an accessible version of the project's technical and project-management documentation without requiring users to access local files.

A link to the deployed MkDocs documentation was added to the project's README.md so that team members, lecturers, and other reviewers can access the documentation directly from the Gitea repository.

The documentation deployment therefore replaced the previous plan of using Cloudflare Pages.

docs.title: 6. Current Outstanding Work
docs.text:
The following items remain as future improvements or later-phase functionality rather than unresolved requirements from the completed Intermediate user stories:

# Feature Status 1 Google Calendar API integration Done — due dates sync to Google Calendar (FEAT-001) 2 Further improvements to notification functionality Done — automatic reminders with push notifications (US28) 3 Further accessibility testing and WCAG improvements Future improvement (FEAT-006); a reduced-motion guard has been added 4 Additional automated unit tests for complex business logic Done — unit tests cover expressions, automation rules, computed fields and more

Statuses updated 2026-09-28.

The Intermediate user stories themselves have been completed and integrated into the project.

docs.title: [Date: 2026-09-18] — Client Meeting & Technical Feedback
docs.text:
• Channel: Client meeting.

  • Feedback:

  • The application is currently slow, so the team should investigate changing the deployment platform and deploy the application using Vercel.

  • The team should use MantisBT as the bug-tracking system to formally document and manage reported bugs.
  • The dashboard currently contains statistics that may be unnecessary because the application already has a separate statistics feature accessible through the side navigation. The team should consider removing the statistics section from the dashboard to avoid duplication.
  • The database was reviewed and it was identified that the tags table is missing. This is affecting the functionality of tags and preventing logbook entries from being updated correctly.
  • The missing tags table may also be contributing to the application's performance issues. The team should investigate possible glitches or delays in communication between the frontend and backend.
  • The team must properly document the internal APIs, including the available endpoints and their purpose, as required by the project.

  • The team needs to set up CI/CD so that testing and code coverage can be automated rather than relying on manually running tests and checking the coverage results.

  • Action Taken / Planned Actions:

  • Investigate and migrate the application deployment to Vercel to address the application's performance issues.

    • Status (2026-09-28). The deployment has not moved: the frontend is still on Cloudflare Pages and the backend on Render. The slowness was tackled in the code instead — see the performance item below.
  • Set up MantisBT and use it as the team's formal bug-tracking system.
    • Superseded (2026-09-25). The team chose a dedicated Gitea project instead; see the next meeting.
  • Remove the duplicated statistics section from the dashboard while keeping the dedicated statistics functionality accessible through the side navigation.
    • Done (2026-09-27). The dashboard's three statistics panels — Active Projects, Entries This Week and Total Time Logged — were removed, and the Statistics page in the side navigation is unchanged. The activity chart was kept: it shows the last seven days as working context rather than repeating a figure the Statistics page reports.
  • Add the missing tags table to the database and ensure that tags are correctly integrated with logbook entries.
    • Done. The tags, project_tags and entry_tags tables exist and are part of the migration baseline.
  • Investigate and resolve possible frontend–backend communication glitches and performance issues.
    • Done (2026-09-28). Pages that sent one request per project now use a single request, the Entries page loads entries in pages, and database indexes were added for the common queries (US33).
  • Document the project's internal APIs, including endpoints, requests, responses, and their purpose.
    • Done. Every endpoint is documented in the API Reference.
  • Set up a CI/CD pipeline to automatically run tests and generate/check code coverage.
    • Done for CI. Gitea Actions typechecks, lints, runs both test suites with coverage and posts the coverage on each commit. Deployment is still done by hand.
  • Continue documenting technical decisions and client feedback as project evidence.

docs.title: [Date: 2026-09-25] — Client Meeting & Feature Feedback
docs.text:

  • Feedback:

  • The client suggested adding a streak feature to show users their consistency in creating logbook entries.

  • The application should show the number of entries per month so users can track their activity over time.

  • Investigate adding progress tracking for entries over time.
  • Implement tag ranking/usage statistics, including most-used tags and the number of entries associated with each tag.
  • Add functionality to compare statistics across different weeks.
    • Done (all five above). The dashboard offers streak, entries-per-month, progress-over-time, tag-ranking and week-comparison panels.
  • Allow users to select the statistics they want displayed.

    • Done (both). Students choose and arrange their dashboard panels, including their own saved statistics, and the layout is kept on the server (US25, US26).
  • Expand the available entry filtering options.
    • Partly done. Entries can be filtered by project, tag, week, overdue and archive state, and filters can be saved. Searching inside custom fields and combining filters are in the Sprint 3 backlog (US36, US37).

    • Not started. Tag names are suggested as you type, and recurring entries (US27) cover work that repeats on a schedule, but entries are not yet completed from earlier ones.

    • Done. Custom expressions and saved statistics were delivered (US22, US23).
